coursework.summary: AI assistance in coursework must be explicitly permitted by the instructor. Check the assignment rules; sample AI-FREE/AS-UA policies and tool listings do not grant permission in other courses.

exams.summary: The current Code prohibits unauthorized AI assistance in exams and restricts in-class assistance to what the exam or proctor provides. Understand the exact assessment conditions. Earlier courses and graduate/honor-code procedures have separate rules.

ai_disclosure.summary: The undergraduate guide requires attribution when AI use is permitted, including quoting verbatim output and acknowledging paraphrases under instructor rules. Communication PhD A/B work separately requires disclosure of AI-assisted language/grammar changes and committee discussion.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Do not put confidential, proprietary, regulated or sensitive Cornell data into public AI. The committee report's training-data warning concerns third-party services; approved platforms have product-specific limits. Copilot Basic is Low Risk only; the limited AI Platform pilot lists Moderate Risk and below.

approved_tools.summary: Firefly needs an Adobe licence; Cornell AI Platform is a limited free pilot; Copilot Basic is free for eligible affiliates aged 18+ with Low Risk data. Zoom AI Companion security/privacy are still being evaluated in the Hub entry. Tool access is not assessment permission.

research_guidance.summary: The 2023 research task-force report is non-binding advice. Communication PhD A/B exam papers/dissertations have specific AI drafting restrictions and disclosure/committee requirements; these are not a Cornell-wide thesis ban. Check applicable research, IRB, sponsor and publication requirements separately.

academic_integrity.summary: The Code explicitly covers unauthorized AI and fabricated citations. Findings require clear and convincing evidence; notice, response and review stages apply. Accepting Responsibility is voluntary and waives ordinary appeals. CTI discourages unreliable detectors; no detector score or AI use alone establishes guilt or an automatic sanction.

teaching_guidance.summary: Communicate course and assignment AI rules clearly. Instructors choose the permitted scope. The 2023 committee does not recommend AI summative grading; this is guidance, not a universal disciplinary prohibition.

security_procurement.summary: Public AI cannot receive sensitive Cornell data. IT requires administrative AI use to comply with its administration guidance; approved/local tools and data classifications require separate checks. The research report alone is not procurement approval.

named_ai_services.summary: Named service listings have separate access, cost, pilot and review conditions; they do not require anyone to use AI.

policy_presence.summary: The Code effective August 24, 2026 explicitly regulates unauthorized AI; course and unit rules remain relevant. Earlier-course cases and graduate/honor-code procedures must be distinguished.
